'expected' is what extract() SHOULD produce for this exact anchor occurrence; qism is recorded for documentation but is NOT part of score_gold.py's headline precision/recall (qism isn't consumed by any downstream table/view yet -- see DAILY_REVIEW.md backlog 'Qism-level (article-part) grain'). Batch 1 (gold_id 0-49, seed 20260920, built 2026-09-20): read window-by-window against the raw Uzbek text and citation_extractor.py's own stop-word/anchor rules (see DAILY_REVIEW.md 2026-09-20 log entry for the reasoning behind each verdict, especially the self_reference-without-article-number 'correctly empty' cases and the gazette-locator 'correctly bare act' cases). Every record is 'verdict: correct' -- this batch found no new extractor bug (the first sample in this project's 9-session sampling history not to). Batch 2 (gold_id 50-99, seed 20260922, built 2026-09-22, disjoint from batch 1): same read-by-hand method. 49/50 records are 'verdict: correct'; one (gold_id 52, row 46605) is 'verdict: known_gap' -- a documented, unfixed extractor limitation (a LexUZ 'paragrafi'->'paragrifi' misspelling isn't recognized as the paragraf unit word) recorded with its true expected output so it scores as an honest recall miss rather than being silently marked correct. See DAILY_REVIEW.md 2026-09-22 log entry and Backlog. Batch 3 (gold_id 100-139, built 2026-09-25, drawn by build_gold_sample_novel.py's signature-stratified sampler instead of a fourth uniform-random batch -- see DAILY_REVIEW.md 2026-09-25 for why): 38/40 'verdict: correct' (including one real bug this batch found and fixed at the source, gold_id 108), 2/40 'verdict: known_gap' (a Roman-numeral chapter+paragraf section-grain loss, gold_id 123; the pre-existing qism-grain limitation now also measured in comma-list form, not just the previously-known dash-range form, gold_id 131).
